title: Pre-Suasion
author: Robert Cialdini
thesisParagraph: The practical argument is that persuasion begins before the request arrives. What a person is noticing, feeling, comparing, or identifying with at the moment of contact changes what the later message can mean. The skill is not to overpower judgment, but to prepare the ground ethically by directing attention toward a true, relevant idea that makes the next choice easier to see.

coreIdeas.name: Prepare the ground
coreIdeas.oneSentence: A request lands differently when the audience has already been oriented toward the right concern.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Look upstream from the ask and decide what should be salient before the ask is made.

coreIdeas.name: Attention gives weight
coreIdeas.oneSentence: What is focal at decision time feels important, explanatory, and worth acting on.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Separate actual importance from attention-created importance before making or shaping a choice.

coreIdeas.name: Some cues pull harder
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Threat, difference, goals, self-relevance, unfinished business, and mystery can seize or hold attention before reasoning starts.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Choose cues that legitimately match the decision instead of decorating the message with noise.

coreIdeas.name: Associations carry meaning
coreIdeas.oneSentence: A focal idea borrows force from the meanings, feelings, places, and traces around it.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Inspect what the setting and nearby concepts are already saying before adding more words.

coreIdeas.name: Principles can be frontloaded
coreIdeas.oneSentence: The classic influence principles work better when the moment first makes the right principle mentally available.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Pick the principle that honestly fits the choice, then make that principle visible before the request.

coreIdeas.name: Unity is deeper than liking
coreIdeas.oneSentence: People become more receptive when they experience the communicator as part of the same We.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Create legitimate togetherness through identity cues or shared action before asking for support.

coreIdeas.name: Ethics protects the effect
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Pre-suasive skill becomes self-defeating when it manipulates people or corrodes trust.
coreIdeas.mentalMove: Run the tactic through an ethics check before the attention plan, then help the new choice last.

targetReader: A manager, seller, teacher, advocate, designer, parent, or professional who needs people to notice the right thing before a decision and who wants influence that survives scrutiny.

signatureMoves: teaches through named influence principles and clean experimental setups
uses compliance-professional stories to reveal a psychological lever
keeps the prose orderly, amused, and empirically anchored
distinguishes ethical alertness from cynical manipulation
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make persuasion sound like charisma magic.
Do not use an influence principle without the trigger condition.

voiceSpecimens: The message starts before the sentence arrives.
Attention prepares the ground where persuasion will stand.
voiceAntiSpecimens: This section will teach readers an important persuasion strategy.
Leverage attention optimization to maximize stakeholder alignment across contexts.
The key takeaway is simple: always be strategic before communicating.
Use this hack whenever you want someone to say yes.
Pre-suasion is basically about vibes and first impressions.
Try this now: set a timer and reflect on how attention affects your life.
teachingArc: The teaching arc starts with the discovery that the before-moment matters, then narrows into how attention creates importance and causal meaning. It then names the cues that seize and hold attention, shows how association and setting do part of the message work, turns the classic influence principles into frontloaded shortcuts, deepens the argument through unity, and ends by putting ethical limits and durability around the whole practice.
forbiddenMoves: Do not turn pre-suasion into a bag of manipulative sales tricks.
Do not invent research details beyond the frozen support sidecars.
Do not treat attention as proof that something is true or good.
Do not collapse unity into ordinary friendliness or team morale.
Do not make ethics a small disclaimer after a clever tactic has already been praised.
Do not teach persuasion as a bag of tricks.
Do not omit the defensive lesson for the reader.
